project.domain: document AI and administrative review workflows

thesis: Uploaded documents are untrusted evidence, never instruction authority; tenant, role, policy and release authority remain outside the model.

evidence.claim: Agent workflows prepare bounded findings and hand-offs rather than granting release authority.
Authority stays outside the model and autonomous funding/legal decisions are prohibited.
Controlled-production paths bind actor/role and fail closed on missing readiness context.
Production readiness and authority boundaries are regression-tested.
Controlled-production document/case state is tenant-scoped.
Postgres storage behavior is integration-tested.
Prepared outcomes remain behind explicit human/policy release authority.
Bounded workflow behavior and review hand-offs are tested.
PDF intake preserves fingerprints and structured document evidence.
Versioned rules and source-linked retrieval remain inspectable.
Untrusted documents are scanned for prompt injection, credential requests and external-action instructions.
Malicious document fixtures are quarantined while benign negative controls remain allowed.
Agent/tool workflows are bounded and produce visible traces.
Agent workflow boundaries are covered by tests.
Review findings, prepared actions and release boundaries remain inspectable.
Durable document/case state supports reproducible review.
External model/provider and deployment-specific security acceptance remain explicitly unproven.
Security classification is regression-tested across the 12-case document benchmark.
The benchmark contains ten benign controls and two explicit prompt-injection/exfiltration documents.
Controlled-production readiness is fail-closed, but real operating SLO/security telemetry remains external evidence.

residualRisks: Regex/document scanning is defense-in-depth telemetry, not proof that indirect prompt injection is solved.
The current 12-case security benchmark is small and synthetic.
A stronger next proof is live-model replay with malicious PDFs, poisoned retrieval context and tool-effect attempts.
Target DMS/Fachverfahren integration, deployment-specific privacy/security acceptance and measured operating SLOs remain unproven.
No autonomous legal, funding or benefit decision is authorized by this posture.
